components: Add-on board on a yellow Kapton base, chip markings scraped off
Bundle of enamelled copper wires hand-soldered to the Nano X board
Replacement battery, with the add-on board taped to it
Loose copper wire running along the battery
implant.notes: The photos and video show an add-on board connected to the Nano X main board by hand-soldered enamelled copper wires. The add-on is taped to a replacement battery, and a loose copper wire runs alongside. This matches the older, hand-wired generation of the implant. Purchase details and the exact generation are not confirmed. The video was posted twice, and both copies are identical frame for frame.

sources.author: Digital Pro
sources.text: @wiimee (the same video, in reply to a post about two Ledgers with no implants found)

images.caption: The Nano X main board, with enamelled copper wires soldered across it to the add-on board, which is taped to a replacement battery.
The add-on board on the battery, with its chip markings scraped off, next to the USB-C connector.
The main board from the other side, with the wire bundle running up to the add-on board and battery.
The battery and add-on board folded onto the main board, with a loose copper wire running along the battery. The Nano X case is in the background.
